title: Depth wire format: header codec and zstd depth payload, shared by depthd and the Pi bridge
requirement: (1) depth_wire.hpp/.cpp depend only on the C++17 standard library and libzstd (no rclcpp, no OpenCV, no ZeroMQ) and compile with gcc 8.4 (Jetson) and the Jazzy toolchain; ros2_common_cpp's library includes them and depthd compiles the same .cpp. (2) A message is ZeroMQ multipart: [topic frame, header, payload]; topic `depth` and `fused` carry zstd-compressed little-endian uint16 mm (0 = invalid), `rgb` carries one JPEG. The header is a versioned little-endian binary layout (my call, the design leaves it to the builder): magic `DPW1`, version, kind, sequence, capture_realtime_ns (left), right_minus_left_ns, width, height, frame_id (up to 63 bytes), camera intrinsics K[9], D[5], rectified P[12], baseline_m, calibrated flag, and Jetson health fields (pipeline_fps, stage_ms for capture/rectify/match/post/mono/encode, pairs_dropped_total, gpu_temp_c, nvgpu_errors_total). Fields are written field by field, never by memcpy of a struct. (3) decode rejects (returns an error, never a partial header) a wrong magic, an unknown version, a truncated buffer, a width*height that does not match the decompressed payload, and an unknown topic. (4) test_depth_wire.cpp covers: header round trip of every field, depth round trip preserving 0 and 65535, zstd payload smaller than raw for a smooth synthetic image, each rejection case, and the rgb message carrying the JPEG bytes unchanged. (5) package.xml declares libzstd-dev; shared/README.md documents the format and that it is the one definition used by jetson/depthd and nodes/jetson_bridge_cpp.
value: Both boards speak one tested wire format, so the depth and RGB streams cannot drift apart.
notes: If rosdep has no libzstd-dev key in the cpp-node-test image, add the apt package to scripts/cpp-node-test.Dockerfile in this task (and say so). Ports are the design's 5550 and 8090.
verify: scripts/cpp-node-test.sh ros2_common_cpp

title: Stereo capture with nvarguscamerasrc, AE/AWB lock, timestamp pairing and the RGB JPEG branch
requirement: (1) Each sensor runs `nvarguscamerasrc sensor-id=<id> sensor-mode=<1640x1232 mode>` with ee-mode 0 and tnr-mode 1, nvvidconv scaling to processing size GRAY8 inside NVMM, into an appsink; the left pipeline tees a second branch nvvidconv -> nvjpegenc (quality rgb.jpeg_quality, rgb.width x rgb.height) -> appsink, throttled to rgb.fps without extra CPU copies. (2) After capture.settle_frames frames the capture sets aelock and awblock on both sources (lock_exposure_after_settle) and logs the locked exposure and gain once. (3) zero_copy true maps NVMM buffers to CUDA through nvbuf_utils (ExtractFdFromNvBuffer, NvEGLImageFromFd, cuGraphicsEGLRegisterImage) into cv::cuda::GpuMat without a CPU copy; zero_copy false uses a system-memory appsink and an upload (both paths exist; the default is measured in T16). (4) Timestamps come from the nvarguscamerasrc buffer metadata (CLOCK_MONOTONIC ns) when present, else the buffer PTS plus base time; they are converted to CLOCK_REALTIME by an offset sampled at start and refreshed every second (chrony keeps realtime on the Pi's clock). (5) StereoPairer pairs nearest timestamps, emits a pair only when |left-right| <= pair_window_ms, drops and counts the rest (skew and orphan counters), never reuses a frame, keeps at most 3 frames per side, and records a skew histogram (buckets 1,2,4,8,16,33 ms). (6) A camera that delivers no frame for 2 s raises a camera_error state (read by /health) and no pair is emitted; there is never a placeholder frame. (7) test_pairing.cpp covers in-window pairing, out-of-window drop, orphan drop, ordering with jitter, the bounded queues and the histogram; test_capture_pipeline.cpp pins the generated pipeline descriptions (elements, sensor ids, mode, ee/tnr, the jpeg branch) for both zero_copy settings. README documents capture, locking and pairing.

requirement: (1) Stages in order, each switchable by config at runtime and timed with CUDA events: left-right consistency (|dL(x) - dR(x - dL)| > lr_check.max_diff invalid; uses the matcher's native LR check when supports_lr_check() and otherwise computes the right disparity), confidence/uniqueness masking, a GPU speckle filter (connected regions below speckle.max_size within max_diff invalidated), cv::cuda::DisparityBilateralFilter guided by the left image, edge-aware hole fill of invalid regions no larger than hole_fill.max_hole_px only (larger holes stay 0), and the ximgproc WLS filter on the CPU (off by default). (2) TemporalFilter: a per-pixel EMA (alpha) on valid pixels, reset per pixel where the grey frame difference exceeds motion_threshold (motion measured by frame difference, no odometry, D4); it never turns an invalid pixel valid on its own. (3) Disabled stages cost nothing measurable (no kernel launch). (4) test_postprocess.cpp: LR check invalidates an injected mismatch, speckle removes a small blob and keeps a large region, hole fill fills a 5x5 hole and leaves a 30x30 hole at 0, bilateral keeps a step edge within 1 px, toggles honoured; test_temporal.cpp: static scene noise drops, a moved region resets, invalid stays invalid. README documents each stage and its knobs.

(3) test_jetson_e2e_check.py tests the metrics-text parsing, rate and p95-from-buckets maths, chrony parsing and each verdict branch on synthetic inputs (no network).
